name: Pharaoh
overview: Pharaoh is a male figure identified as the ruler of Egypt during the lifetime of Joseph. His title and role are noted without specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details. The record emphasizes his position as the Pharaoh during a significant period in Genesis.
namesAndTitles: This individual is referred to by the title 'Pharaoh,' as noted in Genesis 37:36, and also as 'King of Egypt' in Genesis 40:1. The title 'King of Egypt' explicitly denotes his role as the sovereign ruler of the Egyptian nation, though the exact meaning of 'Pharaoh' is not provided in the text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for this person beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as Pharaoh during Joseph's time. There are no additional familial connections documented in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Pharaoh's significance lies in his role as the ruler of Egypt during a pivotal time in the biblical narrative, specifically in the life of Joseph. His position sets the stage for the unfolding of God's providential plan through Joseph's rise to power. Pharaoh's interaction with Joseph marks a key moment in the history of God's people and His unfolding redemptive work.
